I read pp. 102-103 and Defs 6.4/6.5 and the Lean sources. All four clauses are stated: (i) meanCross_class gives W_{α+μ−1/2} at j ≠ 0 with the mean in IncrementBounds (radial M_{μ+1}, others M_μ); (ii) mixed_wave_class gives W_{α+β−κ} for the symmetric same-carrier transport; (iii) transport_mean_class gives M_{α+β−κ} per ordered product, and the sum follows by MemClass.add; (iv) cross-label transport vanishes (supported_transport_zero; chain form transport_zero_of_disjoint_on). HarmonicResidual.transport includes the frame and phase terms. Differences are packaging, explicit context hypotheses and class encoding, each recoverable. All three voters agreed on OK; I only correct the pairing skeptic's claim that clause (iv) is unused at transport level.

findings.summary: No single declaration bundles Lemma 9.2 and no docstring cites it. The four clauses are separate theorems; interactionBlock_uniform packages only (i) and (ii), with an extra (b·∇)b term and a min of exponents.

The zero-harmonic clause is stated only for one ordered transport (transport_mean_class, every m). The symmetric sum is never stated, and the declaration has no callers; Lean's mean equations use covariances.

Lean's W and M classes hold only smoothness and jet bounds on the strip domain. supp ⊂ Ω_γ, smooth zero extension and the 0 ≤ v ≤ L_s restriction are outside the class; support of product harmonics is proved separately.

Lean makes the paper's context explicit as hypotheses: κ ≤ 1/2, phase normal in class 0, k and kp of order ε^(-1/2), 0 ≤ P ≤ 1, ζ ≤ 1, zero stored zero mode, finite band. 'Curl-generated' becomes per-mode solenoidality.

Skeptic's claim: the transport form of the distinct-label clause is unused, and the chain uses it only for covariances. The three named theorems do have no callers, but the chain uses a sibling transport statement.
